title: Dirk Jenter, MIT 15.402 Finance Theory II — Capital Structure I (Spring 2003)
use: Primary teaching reference for the no-friction financing benchmark, identical total state payoffs, value additivity, replication and the question of which omitted friction changes value. Scoped to slides 5–6 and 10–20; original chapter cases and arithmetic are independently derived.
verification: Opened the official course resource and actual 10-page PDF, read the stated scoped slide text and proof. No historical industry debt ratios, source cases or realized-return table is reused as current evidence. This is not a claim of having inspected the original 1958 article.

title: Dirk Jenter, MIT 15.402 Finance Theory II — Capital Structure II (Spring 2003)
use: Primary teaching reference for the leverage/required-return objection to cheap-debt reasoning, financing cash taxes, incremental distress costs, debt overhang, restructuring incentives, anticipated risk taking and conditional trade-off analysis. Scoped to slides 3–15 and 25–44; all payoff contracts and exercises in the chapter are original.
verification: Opened actual 28-page PDF and read the scoped sections, including old-claimholder benefits from investment and creditor anticipation at issue. Extracted equations with incomplete formatting were reconstructed independently. Historical tax-law rules, distress percentages, firm cases and broad prescriptive statements are not adopted as current facts. The perpetual shield shortcut is used only to explain its restrictive assumptions, not to value the finite lab.

title: Dirk Jenter, MIT 15.402 Finance Theory II — Capital Structure: Informational and Agency Considerations (Spring 2003)
use: Primary teaching reference for information-sensitive financing, existing-owner incentives, investment forgone during an equity issue, conditional investor inference, safe-debt contrast and the pecking-order hypothesis. Scoped to slides 6–17 and 19–20; the chapter separately checks its original candidate issue/no-issue equilibrium.
verification: Opened actual 10-page PDF and read the scoped slide bodies. The chapter does not copy its numerical cases, historic financing shares or announcement-return statistics and does not treat its financing hierarchy or announcement direction as universal. No claim that full private-information equilibrium theory is proved.
